policy: The Greek name Jacob is borne by two men in the New Testament, the patriarch and the father of Joseph (MAT 1:15-16), so its number alone names neither. A word names the man its verse names: in 'the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob' and 'the house of Jacob' that is the patriarch, as Abraham and Isaac beside him are; where Jacob stands for the people descended from him, as the verse's Israel does, the word names the people.
source: Essenthos, the Greek Jacob in seven New Testament verses, read by an agent on the lead's instruction, 2026-10-09

rulings.why: MAT 22:32: Jesus quotes Exodus 3:6, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob', the three patriarchs by name; Abraham and Isaac beside him are the patriarchs, and Jacob the son of Matthan (MAT 1:15) is not in view.
MRK 12:26: God's words to Moses at the bush, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:6), name the patriarch with his father and grandfather.
LUK 20:37: Moses at the bush 'calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:6), the patriarch with his father and grandfather.
ACT 3:13: Peter's 'the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers' names the patriarchs, the fathers of the people he speaks to.
ACT 7:32: Stephen quotes the voice at the bush, 'I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:6), after telling Jacob's own story in 7:8-15.

ACT 7:46: David 'desired to find a tabernacle for the house of Jacob' (the King James, from another Greek reading, 'for the God of Jacob'); either way the word is the name of the patriarch whose house or whose God it is, as Luke 1:33's 'the house of Jacob' already names him.

ROM 11:26: 'There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob' (Isaiah 59:20) is said of 'all Israel' at the head of the same verse, the people whose sins God takes away in 11:27; the man Jacob is not in view, so the word names the people descended from him, as the verse's Israel does.
